dedupe_keys.name: open building footprint bias evaluation scripts

description: This archived Python project measures bias in open building-footprint datasets. It compares candidate polygons with user-supplied reference footprints using intersection over union, with a default threshold of 0.5, and counts true positives, false positives and false negatives. Other scripts plot omission rates against study-area attributes and fit weighted regression, with building density as a default weight. The workflow writes Excel tables at building and study-area levels. A modeller could use these error measures before turning a footprint layer into building-exposure or service-demand inputs. No candidate or reference footprint data are distributed with the scripts; users must provide those layers and sensitive study-area variables, then adjust file paths and column names. GitHub marks the project archived and reports AGPL-3.0 for its code. This review did not inspect source code beyond its published paths, run the scripts or test whether their matching assumptions fit a particular city. The method measures agreement with a chosen reference, whose own omissions may matter. Related resources are the evaluated footprint inventories and independent reference layers. For simulation, measured omission rates can guide uncertainty scenarios for the footprint inventory, subject to the chosen reference layer.
licence: AGPL-3.0 for repository code; user-supplied building and reference datasets have separate rights.
